strength: Spin-any-orbit is a real decision (self-spin-only ablation loses by 10-18 points in the base game, 26-34 in the win-at-end variant) and Comet beats Giant passes its ablation; the kinetic gearbox feel matches the owner's vision.
weakness: The win patterns are dead: a formed orbit survives to its owner's turn 0-0.2% of the time, so 95-100% of games end in Long Night at 40-47 turns, with 30-59 captures per game of pure churn. Repeats L3, L1 (Rebound, Recall, Deep Space inert) and L8 (4p fails).
required_changes: Win check at the end of your own turn with a per-count Critical Mass knob (moves pattern wins from under 5% to 15-50% each, Long Night from 95-100% to 15% or less, turns to 14-34)
Shorten the Deck to about 32-36 cards or use 3 opening bodies (turns to 20-30, minutes to about 12), after change 1
Cut Rebound; try a one-turn shield on newly launched bodies (captures per game 59/43/30 toward 15-25, runaway at or below 65%, 4p greedy-vs-strategic gap)
Test captured bodies to Deep Space as an alternative arm (churn), noting it weakens cards changing owners
Re-run all ablations at every count; cut or sharpen Recall and Deep Space; add a keep-a-Giant defence bot; fix 3-4p Long Night tie rate
Per-count knobs: 2p threshold so games do not end in 5 turns; drop 4p if it cannot reach band
revision_reason: The core passes its twist ablations, the diagnosis is clear (win timing), and one tested variant is near band at 3p; stop if cycle 1 does not bring 3p Long Night under 30%.
